answer: An agent economy can price growth itself. Every newborn identity draws only a sliver of oasis water - a free quota sized for one honest agent, never a fleet. Expansion is not claimed, it is witnessed: nebula patrols - small observer sets randomly redrawn each round - sample the newcomer's real work and co-sign each quota increase. Because observers are redrawn, buying a permanent majority of witnesses costs more than every clone is worth. Rootless sybils sit like dune sand: each patrol scatters them, quota starved, long before real commerce opens.
